To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Anton machine has enabled the first MD simulations that have been long enough and accurate enough to provide insights into the mechanisms of important biological processes.
we designed and built a machine that is capable of performing molecular dynamics simulations that are 10 times faster than those that can be run on a conventional computer.

we have designed and built a special-purpose machine called Anton, that is capable of performing molecular dynamics simulation of biological macromolecules at a rate of 1,500,000,000 atoms per second, that is, 100,000 times faster than the best general-purpose computers, and that is capable of simulating biological macromolecules for 100,000,000 times longer than the fastest general-purpose computer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new algorithms for molecular dynamics and their implementation on special-purpose hardware.
the development of a new special-purpose computer, Anton, for the acceleration of long-time-scale molecular dynamics simulations of biological macromolecules.
the development of a novel, massively parallel computer system, Anton, that is designed specifically for the purpose of long-time molecular dynamics simulations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current state of the art in MD simulation is not yet sufficient for the simulation of the biologically relevant time scales.
the current state-of-the-art in MD simulation technology has reached its practical limits.
, while the current state of the art is impressive and has already provided many important results, it is far from being able to address many of the questions that are of the greatest interest.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a special-purpose computer architecture that can simulate a molecular system of about 100,000 atoms for 1 millisecond.
we have designed and constructed a special-purpose molecular dynamics machine called Anton.

we have developed a special-purpose machine, called Anton, for molecular dynamics simulation that is capable of performing simulations of biological molecules on time scales on the millisecond time scale, and that we have demonstrated its ability to perform simulations on time scales of 10-50 micro-seconds.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, with careful engineering, the performance of a special-purpose machine designed for a specific class of problems can be orders of magnitude greater than that of the fastest general-purpose computer.
the performance of Anton is sufficient to allow the simulation of proteins on the millisecond timescale.

, in principle, the time scale of current MD simulations can be increased by about an order of magnitude by using a new, highly optimized MD code, Anton, and by using a new MD algorithm, the No-U-turn sampler, which we call No-U-turn Molecular Dynamics (NAMD).
